actions.title: Playbook — Henry Fletcher (UI/UX designer)
actions.body:
# Playbook — Henry Fletcher, Senior UI/UX Product Designer

Last updated: 2026-11-16

## Standards we follow

1. **WCAG 2.2 Level AA is the compliance target.** WCAG 3.0 is still a draft and W3C states it does not replace WCAG 2. Source: [W3C WAI news, 3 Mar 2026](https://www.w3.org/WAI/news/2026-03-03/wcag3) (as relayed by search; page not opened).
2. **Every screen specifies all states:** empty, loading, error, disabled, focus, and long Arabic and English strings (house rule, agent profile).
3. **RTL is designed, not mirrored.** Direction-sensitive items (icons, progress, carousels, numerals, safe-area insets) are specified explicitly (house rule).
4. **Visual decisions are tokens.** Prefer the DTCG format so tokens stay tool-neutral. Format, Color and Resolver modules 2025.10 are a Final Community Group Report (not a W3C Standard). Source: [DTCG announcement, 28 Oct 2025](https://w3.org/community/design-tokens/2025/10/28/design-tokens-specification-reaches-first-stable-version/); spec at [designtokens.org/tr/2025.10](https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/).
5. **Light and dark mode, plus a 360 px layout, are requirements**, checked on rendered output, not only by token arithmetic.
6. Reference sets (from docs/learning-resources.md): NN/g, Material Design 3, Apple HIG, WCAG 2.2 quick reference, Laws of UX.

## What's new

- **EN 301 549 V4.1.1 (published 2 Sep 2026)** moves the web requirements from WCAG 2.1 to WCAG 2.2 A/AA, per commentary. Official Journal citation was expected in November; not confirmed. Until confirmed, design to WCAG 2.2 AA anyway. Source: [Davis Wright Tremaine, Sep 2026](https://www.dwt.com/insights/2026/09/european-accessibility-act-ict-standards-update) (secondary, not opened).
- **Baseline: `field-sizing`** (form controls that grow with content) became Baseline Newly available, per the June 2026 digest. Check support before specifying auto-growing text areas. Source: [web.dev, June 2026 digest](https://web.dev/blog/baseline-digest-jun-2026?hl=en) (via search summary).
- **Baseline monthly digests continue.** The August 2026 digest was published 28 Sep 2026, and the July one added a Baseline audit to Lighthouse (10 Aug 2026). Contents not read. Source: [Aug 2026 digest](https://web.dev/blog/baseline-digest-aug-2026), [Jul 2026 digest](https://web.dev/blog/baseline-digest-jul-2026).
- **WCAG 3 working draft, 3 Mar 2026** (older than 3 months, kept for context). Sources conflict about a later draft; none confirmed. Source: [W3C TR](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/WD-wcag-3.0-20260303/).

## Lessons from our projects

- **todo-app review:** the 22 px checkboxes pass only because they sit inside a 44x44 label. Specify the label as the target, not the glyph.
- **todo-app F-4:** `padding-inline-start` mapped to `safe-area-inset-left` swaps the insets in RTL. Specify safe-area insets as physical values, or swap them under `[dir=rtl]`.
- **todo-app F-5:** a language button named only "English" or "العربية" has a weak accessible name. Spec "Language: English"-style labels.
- **todo-app:** the native date picker follows the browser locale, not the page locale, so Arabic UIs can show `mm/dd/yyyy`. Spec a custom or labelled alternative.
- **todo-app:** contrast was verified by calculation only. Native control rendering, placeholder, hover and focus states were not measured. Add them to the design QA list.
- **xo-online N-03:** names interpolated into `aria-label` and share text need bidi isolation. Spec isolation wherever user-supplied names mix scripts.
- **xo-online:** reduced motion, AA contrast (N3) and the 360 px layout (N5) had no recorded check. Every spec must name how each is verified.
- **Both:** WebKit/iOS was never run. Flag Safari input zoom, safe areas and Arabic plural ICU as open risks in every spec.

## Watch list

- Official Journal citation of EN 301 549 V4.1.1 (affects EU client work).
- WCAG 3 progress; do not adopt its conformance model until W3C publishes a stable version.
- Baseline status of anchor positioning and interest invokers (`interestfor`): not confirmed, so do not spec them without a fallback.
- Adoption of DTCG 2025.10 in our token export pipeline (tool support claims are unverified).
- NN/g, Material 3 and Apple HIG updates since August 2026.

*Web access note: only WebSearch worked. WebFetch could not reach w3.org, web.dev or nngroup.com (hosts not allowed), so no page was opened and every item above rests on search summaries. Not checked: NN/g research from Aug to Nov 2026, Material 3 and Apple HIG changes, the content of the Aug 2026 Baseline digest, WCAG 2.2 errata, and RTL-specific guidance updates. Nothing unconfirmed is included.*

Learned: design to WCAG 2.2 AA now (EU standard EN 301 549 V4.1.1 adopts it); our gaps are RTL and rendered checks. Will do differently: every spec names how contrast, reduced motion and RTL get verified.

actions.title: Playbook — James Whitaker (Tech Lead)
actions.body:
# Playbook — James Whitaker, Senior Software Architect & Technical Lead
Last updated: 2026-11-16

## Standards we follow
- **Record every important decision as an ADR** (context, options, decision, consequences) in `docs/decisions/`. MADR 4.0.0 (2024-09-17) is the current template; it has full and minimal variants. Nygard's original template is the alternative. Source: [adr.github.io/madr](https://adr.github.io/madr), [adr.github.io/adr-templates](https://adr.github.io/adr-templates).
- **Design against the OWASP Top 10:2025** (announced Nov 2025; final released Jan 2026 per a search summary). Categories confirmed in sources: A01 Broken Access Control (now includes SSRF), A02 Security Misconfiguration, A03 Software Supply Chain Failures (new), A04 Cryptographic Failures, A05 Injection, A06 Insecure Design, A07 Authentication Failures, A08 Software or Data Integrity Failures, A09 Security Logging & Alerting Failures, A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions (new). Sources: [OWASP Top 10:2025 introduction](https://owasp.org/Top10/2025/0x00_2025-Introduction/), [eSecurity Planet](https://www.esecurityplanet.com/threats/news-owasp-top-10-2025/), [Orca Security](https://orca.security/resources/blog/owasp-top-10-2025-key-changes/). Rule for us: A03 and A10 become explicit review items (dependency and workflow trust; safe failure on malformed input).
- **Treat a public broker as untrusted input.** Every message is validated at the boundary (schema, size, ranges, clock skew, plausibility), not only shape-checked. Application-level integrity checks or payload encryption are the options when the transport has no authentication; TLS alone protects only the link. Source: [HiveMQ, MQTT message data integrity](https://hivemq.com/blog/mqtt-security-fundamentals-mqtt-message-data-integrity), [HiveMQ, payload encryption](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/mqtt-security-fundamentals-payload-encryption/). (Undated pages; read as standing guidance.)
- **Keep the transport behind an interface** (as in xo-online: `Transport` with MQTT, BroadcastChannel and in-memory implementations) so the trust model can change without rewriting the app. This is our own practice, not an external source.
- **Simplicity and $0 first.** Pick the least complex option that meets the NFRs; any paid service goes to the COO.

## What's new
- **Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 35, published 2026-11-04.** Headline theme: "Harness engineering at scale" (the controls, tools and guardrails around coding agents); third-party coverage lists four themes (harnesses, model choice, parallel agents, building an AI factory), not verified against the PDF. Sources: [Thoughtworks Radar](https://www.thoughtworks.com/radar), [Thoughtworks podcast on Vol. 35 themes](https://www.thoughtworks.com/insights/podcasts/technology-podcasts/themes-technology-radar-vol-35), [Thoughtworks blog "Harness is a product"](https://www.thoughtworks.com/insights/blog/generative-ai/harness-is-a-product), [third-party summary](https://braindetox.kr/en/posts/thoughtworks_technology_radar_vol35.html).
- **Thoughtworks Radar Vol. 34, April 2026** (earlier, kept for context): themes include securing permission-hungry agents, putting coding agents on a leash, and combating AI "cognitive debt" by returning to engineering fundamentals. Sources: [Thoughtworks press release](https://www.thoughtworks.com/about-us/news/2026/combat-ai-cognitive-debt-radar-v34), [iTWire](https://itwire.com/business-it-news/data/as-ai-accelerates-software-complexity,-thoughtworks-technology-radar-urges-a-return-to-engineering-fundamentals-to-combat-cognitive-debt).
- **npm supply-chain worms continued in 2026** ("Mini Shai-Hulud": April–May 2026 waves; further cases reported by August 2026). Reported weakness: over-broad trusted-publishing trust policies, and malicious versions that carried valid provenance attestations, so provenance alone is not proof of safety. Counts differ between sources, so none are quoted. Sources: [Cloud Security Alliance research note, 2026-05-14](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-shai-hulud-ai-npm-supply-chain-attack-2026/), [The Hacker News, npm hardening (Feb 2026)](https://thehackernews.com/2026/02/npms-update-to-harden-their-supply.html), [eSecurity Planet](https://www.esecurityplanet.com/news/wormable-malware-triggers-githubs-push-for-stronger-npm-security/). Our controls: committed lockfile, `npm ci`, `npm audit`, minimal dependencies, no publish tokens in the repo.
- **MCP specification 2026-07-28** (final 2026-07-28, release candidate 2026-05-21; slightly over 3 months old): stateless core, hardened OAuth, Dynamic Client Registration deprecated in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents. Relevant if we ever build or consume MCP servers. Sources: [Descope](https://www.descope.com/blog/post/july-2026-mcp-revision), [Agentic AI Foundation](https://aaif.io/blog/authorization-in-mcp-2026-07-28-clarifying-trust-relationships-for-agentic-systems). These are secondary sources; the spec at modelcontextprotocol.io was not read.
- **ADR practice:** no 2026 change to MADR or adr.github.io was found; MADR 4.0.0 (2024-09-17) is still the latest seen.

## Lessons from our projects
- **xo-online (review 2026-11-01/02): a public MQTT broker means every client is a possible attacker.** `parseRoom` first only checked shape; the reviewer showed that huge `version`, far-future timestamps and inconsistent boards could freeze rooms or flood the lobby (F-02). Fix pattern now in the code: bound version and timestamps, check board/turn consistency, cap list and cache sizes, accept the residual (anti-cheat out of scope) in writing. Next time, put these bounds in the first ADR, not after review.
- **Never let a client's local clock authorise destructive actions** (F-03): a viewer with a clock far ahead could clear other people's live rooms. Only seated players may clear; clocks are compared with a sanity bound. The new 10-minute skew limit has a side effect (N-01): a device whose clock is far behind silently ignores its opponent. Design the user-facing message for a rejected-but-valid state.
- **Say in the ADR when we accept a risk, and who accepted it.** F-04 (public broker, open lobby) stayed open until the CEO accepted assumptions A1-A6 via the COO.
- **Evidence over claims:** tests ran only against an in-memory broker, so live behaviour (Last Will, reconnect, latency) stayed "unverified" until a real two-device check. Mark such ADR consequences as unverified.
- **Change of meaning needs a recorded decision** (N-04): a fix changed the AC-7.2 "idle" semantics without a note in the spec. Record behavioural changes made during security fixes in the ADR or spec.
- **todo-app (review 2026-11-01):** storage input is validated with a type guard and nothing is rendered as HTML (no `innerHTML`/`eval`), which is the pattern to repeat; the review's findings were Low and process-related (lint not in CI, stale report text).
- **Release automation is code too:** the xo-online release workflow failed at its report step on a heredoc error. Test workflow steps locally before relying on them.

## Watch list
- Read the full Radar Vol. 35 PDF and list blips relevant to our $0 static-site and PWA stack, including anything in the Caution ring.
- Read the official OWASP Top 10:2025 category pages (A03, A10) and turn them into a short review checklist.
- Check whether the HiveMQ public broker has published usage terms or limits (not found); consider a self-hostable free fallback if the broker changes.
- Verify the MCP 2026-07-28 spec against the official source before any MCP work.
- Verify npm trusted-publishing guidance from GitHub's own changelog before we publish any package.
- Google SRE books and Martin Fowler's site: no new items checked this session.

*Web access note: direct page fetches failed (owasp.org and thoughtworks.com did not resolve in this session), so every item comes from web search results only. The OWASP list was confirmed from search snippets, not the official page; the Radar Vol. 35 PDF, the MCP spec text, and HiveMQ public broker terms could not be read or checked. Anything a search could not confirm is left out.*

Learned: OWASP Top 10:2025 adds supply-chain failures and exceptional-condition handling. Will do differently: treat every public-broker message as hostile input, with bounds and accepted residual risk in the ADR up front.

actions.title: Playbook — Thomas Hughes (Mobile engineer)
actions.body:
# Playbook — Thomas Hughes, Senior Mobile Application Engineer

Last updated: 2026-11-16

## Standards we follow

- **Design for the bad case first.** Slow devices, flaky networks, denied permissions. Every screen has loading, empty, error, offline and permission-denied states.
- **Name the platform and OS** whenever we describe behaviour ("Android 15+ edge-to-edge", "iOS Safari standalone"). Report exactly what we ran and on what (simulator/emulator/OS); say "not run" otherwise.
- **RTL is explicit.** Use logical properties and `I18nManager`; mirror icons by hand. Physical `left/right` is allowed only for hardware insets, and those must be swapped under RTL (see Lessons).
- **Touch and safe areas.** Tap targets at least 44x44 (the visible control may be smaller if it sits inside a 44x44 hit area). Inputs at 16px or larger to avoid iOS zoom. Use `viewport-fit=cover` plus `env(safe-area-inset-*)` on the web, and window insets in native code. Never assume status-bar height.
- **Quality gate before reporting:** unit/component tests for new logic; one low-end Android profile; accessibility labels on interactive elements; no unhandled promise rejections or yellow-box warnings.
- **Tests:** propose Maestro flows for critical journeys and coordinate with the QA Automation Engineer.
- **Boundaries.** Never commit signing keys, keystores or API secrets (this repo is public). Store publishing needs the COO's release approval. **$0 rule: an Apple Developer account ($99/yr) or Google Play account ($25) needs CEO approval, brought by the COO.** Until then we ship PWAs, Expo Go or dev builds, and web previews only.
- Architecture changes go through the Technical Lead.

## What's new

Window checked: 2026-08-16 to 2026-11-16. Items before the window are marked "context" because they set the baseline we build on.

**In the window**
- **Google Play now requires target API 36 (Android 16) for new apps and updates, from 2026-08-31.** Existing apps must target API 35 or higher to stay available to new users on newer Android. Google offered an extension to 2026-11-01 (that date has passed). Wear OS and Automotive need API 35; TV and XR need API 34. Source: [Android Developers, Target API level requirements](https://developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk) (fetched 2026-11-16). Action: set `targetSdkVersion` 36 in new Expo/RN builds and test on an Android 16 emulator.
- **App Store Connect now requires iOS 13 or later as the deployment target, since 2026-09-09.** Source: [Apple Developer, Upcoming requirements](https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/) (fetched 2026-11-16). Action: do not set a lower deployment target.
- **Expo SDK 56 has a known Hermes V1 memory regression** affecting apps that use `react-native-worklets` or `react-native-reanimated`, noted by Expo on 2026-08-27. A later patch reportedly fixes it (`expo@57.0.17` per the SDK 57 notes). Sources: [SDK 56 changelog](https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-56), [SDK 57 changelog](https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-57). I read these through search summaries only, not the pages themselves.
- **Expo SDK 58 exists** and is reported to add iOS 27 support and React Native 0.88. Source: [Expo, How to upgrade to SDK 58](https://expo.dev/blog/how-to-upgrade-to-sdk-58). Release date and breaking changes not confirmed.
- **Maestro CLI 2.9.0 (light and dark mode in one flow), 2.10.0 (`--device-os` accepts a full Android system image path) and 2.11.0 (Android 17 / API 37 support)** are published. Sources: [2.9.0](https://maestro.dev/blog/maestro-cli-2-9-0), [Maestro blog](https://maestro.dev/blog). Release dates not confirmed.

**Context (before the window)**
- Apple: since 2026-04-28 uploads must be built with Xcode 26 or later and the iOS 26 SDK. Source: [Apple Developer, Upcoming requirements](https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/).
- React Native 0.86 (2026-06-11): fixes for Android 15+ edge-to-edge, including when the OS enforces it without the Gradle property; no breaking changes from 0.85; DevTools light/dark emulation. Source: [React Native 0.86](https://reactnative.dev/blog/2026/06/11/react-native-0.86).
- Expo SDK 57 (2026-06-30) moves to React Native 0.86. Source: [Expo SDK 57](https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-57). SDK 55 (2026-02-25) dropped the Legacy Architecture; React Native 0.83 is New Architecture only. Source: [Expo SDK 55](https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-55).
- Android 17 (API 37) behaviour changes for all apps: memory limits by device RAM, background audio-focus limits, SMS OTP protection (use SMS Retriever or SMS User Consent). Source: [Android 17 behavior changes: all apps](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/17/behavior-changes-all). Stable release date not confirmed from an official page.

## Lessons from our projects

- **todo-app review F-4 (Low):** mapping `padding-inline-start` to `safe-area-inset-left` swaps the insets in RTL, because the inline start becomes the right side. Use physical `padding-left/right` with the physical insets, or swap them under `[dir=rtl]`. Source: `projects/todo-app/docs/review.md`.
- **todo-app passed its rendered check** with these patterns: `--tap: 44px`, checkboxes inside a 44x44 label, inputs at `max(1rem,16px)`, `viewport-fit=cover`, `dir="auto"` on user text, and no horizontal scroll at 320px with a 90-character unbroken title. Reuse them.
- **Gap the reviewer flagged:** the review used Chrome only. Not checked: real iPhone/Safari input zoom, notched-device safe areas, Safari private-mode storage, and home-screen web-app mode. Ask for a WebKit or real-device run, or state "not run".
- **xo-online review:** nothing mobile-specific found.

## Watch list

- Google Play target API 37 (Android 17). One secondary source says Google announced August 2027 for new apps and updates. I could not confirm that on an official page, so verify it before planning.
- Expo SDK 58 upgrade path and the iOS 27 SDK requirement for App Store uploads (not announced as far as I could confirm).
- Expo Router no longer allows imports from `@react-navigation/*` (SDK 56 and later); codemod available.
- Hermes V1 memory behaviour with Reanimated and worklets.
- Android 17: SMS OTP flows, memory limits, and CameraX 1.5.2 / 1.6.0+ to avoid a reported crash (third-party report, unconfirmed).
- Maestro: confirm 2.9 to 2.11 changelogs and dates, then update our flows for light/dark testing.

*Web access note: expo.dev, reactnative.dev, maestro.dev, support.google.com, techdevnotes.com and releases.sh could not be fetched (blocked in this session). Only developer.android.com and developer.apple.com were read directly. All other items come from search-result summaries and are marked where dates or details are unconfirmed. Official React Native and Expo changelog pages, the Play Console policy page, and Maestro release dates still need a direct check.*

Learned: Play requires target API 36 since 2026-08-31 and Apple iOS 13+ deployment target since 2026-09-09. Will do differently: set targetSdkVersion 36 in new builds and never claim device checks we did not run.

actions.title: Playbook — Emily Harrington (Frontend engineer)
actions.body:
# Playbook — Emily Harrington, Senior Frontend & Web Engineer
Last updated: 2026-11-16

## Standards we follow
- Semantic HTML and keyboard support first; ARIA only fills real gaps. Every control has an accessible name that includes its visible text.
- CSS logical properties everywhere (`margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline`, `padding-inline`) so RTL works by construction. Exception: `env(safe-area-inset-*)` is physical, so map it per direction (see lessons).
- Every component has loading, empty, error and disabled states. Test at 360px (and 320px), light and dark, English and Arabic.
- Static hosting: no server code, no secrets in the client bundle, no third-party analytics without the COO's approval. $0 only.
- Validate all input (Zod or equivalent); never use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`innerHTML` for user text.
- Names and user text inside sentences get bidi isolation (`<bdi>` or FSI...PDI); strip bidi control characters on input.
- Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`; never convey meaning by colour alone; contrast at WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text and UI).
- Before reporting: lint, typecheck, unit tests, Playwright journey, production build; report real output; say "not run" for anything not run.
- Pin dependency versions that are at least two weeks old; run `npm audit`.

## What's new
Items are dated; "secondary" means a news or vendor site, not the project's own page. Only search results were available (see note), so official pages were not opened.
- **Next.js 16.4** released 2026-10-06 (per a CodeZine report and BuildMVPFast, secondary; the official post lists lazy compilation, smaller Turbopack output, React 19.3 features and Cache Components improvements). Secondary sources say Cache Components become the default for new apps. A security patch is listed on 2026-10-14 (Releasebot, secondary). Action: for any Next.js project, check the installed version against the official security advisory before the next build. Sources: [nextjs.org/blog/next-16-4](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16-4), [CodeZine](https://codezine.jp/news/detail/29959), [Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/vercel/next-js). Most of our work is static Vite + React, so this is awareness, not an action.
- **Baseline, September 2026 roundup** (web.dev, published 2026-10-02): features reaching Baseline Newly available after Safari 27 and Firefox 155-157, including the `progress()` and `alpha()` CSS functions, scroll anchoring, and `cookieStore.set()` `maxAge`. Pairings came from machine-translated copies of the page, so confirm on the English page before using any of them. Source: [web.dev/blog/web-platform-09-2026](https://web.dev/blog/web-platform-09-2026). Action: check Baseline status on MDN or web.dev before using a new CSS or JS feature.
- **Baseline, August 2026 digest** (web.dev, published 2026-09-28): text-box properties and the global `autocorrect` attribute became Baseline Newly available. Source: [web.dev/blog/baseline-digest-aug-2026](https://web.dev/blog/baseline-digest-aug-2026). Action: `text-box-trim`/`text-box-edge` can help with Arabic/Latin vertical alignment in buttons; verify in a render first.
- **Safari 27.0** shipped about 2026-09-14 with iOS 27 and macOS 27 (9to5Mac 2026-09-17, secondary; WebKit's own tally of 83 features and 844 fixes). Action: our reviews have never run on real Safari; run the iPhone pass that the todo-app review requires on Safari 27. Source: [9to5Mac, 2026-09-17](https://9to5mac.com/2026/09/17/webkit-blog-breaks-down-whats-new-with-safari-27-for-developers-including-mcp-support/).
- **Chrome 155 and 156** (Chrome for Developers, WebGPU update dated 2026-10-07; Chrome 156 beta post, date not shown). Source: [developer.chrome.com/blog](https://developer.chrome.com/blog). No action identified.
- **WCAG 3.0 drafts**: Working Draft dated 2026-03-03; the WCAG 3 introduction page says updated drafts were published in September 2026 (contents not confirmed). Still not a compliance standard; WCAG 2.2 AA stays our baseline. Sources: [W3C WAI news 2026-03-03](https://www.w3.org/WAI/news/2026-03-03/wcag3), [WCAG 3 introduction](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG3).

## Lessons from our projects
- **todo-app F-1:** two tabs, last write wins. Listen for the `storage` event on the versioned key and reload state, or document the limitation.
- **todo-app F-2:** do not save on mount. Entries dropped by validation are overwritten and lost; skip the first save or keep a backup key on parse failure.
- **todo-app F-3:** "today" computed per render goes stale across midnight. Recompute on `visibilitychange` or a timer.
- **todo-app F-4:** `padding-inline-start: env(safe-area-inset-left)` swaps in RTL. Use physical left/right for safe-area insets, or swap under `[dir=rtl]`.
- **todo-app F-5:** a language button named only "English" is a weak accessible name. Use "Language: English" (an unused `languageSwitchLabel` already existed). Check that defined strings are actually used.
- **todo-app:** overdue shown by text plus icon, not colour; Arabic plurals via `Intl.PluralRules` with all six CLDR forms (verified in Node ICU only, Safari ICU not run).
- **xo-online F-06 / N-03:** bidi isolation was missed in `aria-label` and share-text strings. Wrap every interpolated name, including attributes and plain strings, with `isolate()`.
- **xo-online F-07:** reduced motion was checked only by stylesheet inspection and a Chromium claim with no stored script. Commit the check script and its output, and test with the OS setting too.
- **xo-online F-03 / F-02:** never let one client's local clock decide to delete shared data; validate and bound every field from an untrusted channel (public MQTT broker).
- **xo-online N-01:** rejecting messages for clock skew fails silently; show a hint when a valid message is rejected for that reason alone.
- **Both:** claims without artifacts count as unverified. Real-device Safari and VoiceOver have not been run yet; say so in every report.
